subject: Runway ledger & exit-safeguard playbook for CareLogic evaluation
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@carelogic.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@carelogic.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial acceptance markers & proposed MAP

Hey Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at CareLogic was impressed with the latency/throughput profile you showed. Before we commit to a pilot, Procurement and our clinical ops team want a clear playbook for how we’ll measure success and what the exit/rollback triggers look like.

Attached is our standard MAP template but I sketched three things we care about most:
- Functional accuracy: our triage assistant must maintain >= 92% concordance with clinician-annotated labels on the provided 300 sample set.
- Safety/fallthrough: any PII or PHI extraction must be redacted and logged; failures must be reproducible.
- Reliability: 99.5% of inference requests during a 72-hour soak should succeed with <= 500ms p50 and <= 900ms p95.

We’re targeting a 6-week evaluation window. Can you confirm Redwood’s acceptance tests and whether you can live with a conditional go/no-go on week 4 if the smoke scenarios fail? Also procurement will need a DPA redline tracker — I’ve cc’d procurement in case they have immediate asks.

Best,
Tom
Procurement Lead, CareLogic Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@carelogic.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial acceptance markers & proposed MAP

Tom — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the MAP template. Replying with a concise runbook that maps your asks to concrete acceptance tests, including where we expect to instrument evidence.

Summary / high-level plan
- Evaluation window: 6 weeks, with a formal checkpoint at week 4 (smoke) and final signoff at week 6.
- Owners: CareLogic clinical ops owns label validation; Redwood owns infrastructure SLAs and evidence capture.
- Deliverables: MAP workbook (attached draft), smoke-scenario harness, and a small acceptance-test corpus (~300 records) to be run blinded.

Key acceptance gates (proposed)
1) Accuracy gate — Functional concordance
- Test: blinded run of the 300-sample corpus.
- Pass: >= 92% agreement with your clinician labels, < 2% gradeable edge-case rate.
- Evidence: scorecard CSV + annotated diffs and sampling of 30 error cases.
2) Safety gate — PII/PHI handling
- Test: credentialed ingestion of 50 masked records with injected synthetic PHI tokens.
- Pass: 0 incidents of unredacted PII in output; all incidents must be reproducible with full audit trail.
- Evidence: redaction logs, audit trace (request/response ids).
3) Reliability gate — Soak and stress
- Test: 72-hour soak at target throughput (defined below) + two controlled spike events.
- Pass: >= 99.5% successful responses; p50 <= 500ms, p95 <= 850ms (we’d like to tighten to 800ms if you can).
- Evidence: telemetry export, tracing spans, error budget report.
4) Operational gate — Observability and rollback
- Test: runbook execution for canary, canary-failure rollback within 15 mins.
- Pass: automated rollback executed in test and a clear owner on-call for incidents.
- Evidence: canary metrics, runbook notes, post-mortem template.

I’ve attached a draft MAP workbook (MAP_CareLogic_v1.xlsx) with fields for owners, schedule, artifacts, and the acceptance-test checklist. Karthik — please add the technical thresholds (latency/throughput, model variants, quantization tolerances) and a minimal smoke-scenario manifest.

If that aligns, propose we book a 30-min alignment call Friday to lock week-4 triggers and the procurement redline path.

— Mateo
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_CareLogic_v1.xlsx (draft)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@carelogic.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial acceptance markers & proposed MAP

Adding the technical acceptance test definitions and thresholds so the MAP is actionable. I kept them conservative but achievable; happy to iterate.

Technical acceptance tests (these will be automated where possible)
- Baseline model variant: redwood-base-13b / quantized int8 (prod-like).
- Latency/throughput
  - Target throughput: 40 concurrent inference sessions, average token output length 60 tokens.
  - Soak thresholds: p50 <= 450ms, p95 <= 850ms, error rate <= 0.5% over 72h.
  - Spike scenario: +3x traffic for 5 minutes; system must keep error rate < 2% and recover to baseline within 10 minutes.
- Fidelity/quality
  - Evaluation: automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not sufficient for task) + human concordance check.
  - Pass condition: automated filters + human sample (30 cases) show no systematic drift; final concordance >= 92%.
- Cache & warmup
  - KV cache warming procedure will be documented; first-request latency allowance for cold-cache tests.
- Observability artifacts
  - Required: token-level latency histogram, top-10 tail-call traces, per-route cost breakdown, and audit logs for every request.
- Rollback/Fail-open behavior
  - If p95 breaches 1.5x threshold or a safety incident occurs (PHI leakage), automatic traffic shift to a fallback variant within 15 minutes.

Open operational questions for CareLogic
1) Are you able to share the 300-sample gold set as hashed/obfuscated records? We need a blinded comparison.
2) For the human concordance check, who will sign off as the clinical owner? (Name + title)
3) Procurement: we will need a DPA redline window of 10 business days to reconcile changes; is that acceptable?

I’ll add all of this to acceptance-smoke-scenarios.md and share a link after internal review.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Runway ledger & exit-safeguard playbook for CareLogic evaluation

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the level of detail. Quick responses to the open Qs:
- We can provide the 300-sample set as a hashed token file and a separate mapping table under an encrypted transfer. Clinical sign-off will be Dr. Emily Chen (Chief Clinical Informatics Officer).
- Procurement: 10 business days for DPA redlines is acceptable; I’ll route the redline tracker to you by EOD Tuesday.

On rollback: we want a clearly defined emergency-stop condition beyond metrics (e.g., any confirmed PHI leakage). If that is triggered, we need the technical contact and executive escalation path documented in the MAP. Can Redwood confirm the on-call contact and the escalation ladder we should use?

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood sends the updated MAP workbook with the technical gates filled in (attaching acceptance-smoke-scenarios.md and the test harness link).
2) Procurement will upload DPA redlines to the shared drive and flag any non-starters.
3) Week 4 smoke checkpoint call: Friday, July 16 — 30 minutes.

If you can send the MAP update and the observability export plan by Wednesday, we’ll start the transfer of the sample set and open the procurement tracker.

Thanks,
Tom
Procurement Lead, CareLogic Health
